1	# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
2	"""The schema's enumerated vocabularies — ONE definition per value set.
3	
4	Every enumerated column in docs.db used to spell its allowed values as a SQL
5	string literal at the CREATE TABLE site, and sometimes a SECOND time as a module
6	constant guarding the declared-config path. That is 25 literals across 8 modules
7	with nothing tying them together, and it had already drifted: `_VALID_KINDS` was
8	defined TWICE with DIFFERENT values (`threads.py`, a set of thread kinds;
9	`locks.py`, a tuple of lock kinds), so a cross-import would have produced a
10	silently wrong CHECK on whichever table lost the race.
11	
12	This module is the single source. A column's allowed values live in exactly one
13	`Vocabulary`; the DDL asks it for a clause (`check(table, column)`) and the
14	declared-config loaders ask the SAME object to validate a token.
15	
16	TRUE LEAF — zero intra-package imports, by design. `doxyguard_db/_common.py`
17	pulls in `rich`, while `doxyguard_db/query/_common.py` is deliberately
18	stdlib-only; importing either here would make one of those two layers
19	un-importable without the other's dependencies. The logger comes from `logging`
20	directly for exactly that reason.
21	
22	FIVE VOCABULARIES SHARE THE TUPLE ('low','medium','high') AND ARE STILL FIVE
23	OBJECTS. They mean five different things — spawn-detection strength, inferred-
24	vs-declared provenance, lock-identity certainty, acquisition-resolution success,
25	and a constant on `external_boundaries`. Binding one object to all five would
26	mean that adding a value for one silently widens the CHECK on the other four,
27	while every test that compares the shipped schema to this registry stays green.
28	
29	GENERATION NEVER USES `{tuple!r}`. The idiom this replaces (`locks.py`) emits
30	`CHECK(c IN ('x',))` for a one-value set — a SQLite SYNTAX ERROR — and
31	`CHECK(c IN ("it's",))` for a value containing an apostrophe. It survived only
32	by accident, because every set it was applied to happened to have >= 2 values;
33	`boundary_source` had exactly one until the declared-dispatch terminus kind
34	landed, which is precisely how a latent one-value case reaches production.
35	`values` is also a TUPLE, never a set: set iteration order is not part of any
36	contract, and a set here would make the shipped schema text vary between builds.
37	
38	FAIL CLOSED on a declared value outside its vocabulary (`validated` raises
39	`DeclarationError`), rather than normalizing to 'unknown' as the loaders used
40	to. `acq_form`/`acq_role`/`acq_mode` have no 'unknown' member at all, so a
41	fallback has to invent a specific, real synchronization claim out of a typo. And
42	`locks.kind` is part of lock IDENTITY (`UNIQUE(name, scope, kind)`), so two
43	differently-typo'd kinds normalizing to one token COLLAPSE INTO ONE lock row —
44	fabricating shared synchronization, which is precisely the error the lock layer
45	documents itself as failing closed against.
46	
47	@brief Central registry of the schema's enumerated value sets.
48	@version 3
49	"""
50	
51	from __future__ import annotations
52	
53	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
54	from pathlib import Path
55	
56	# NOTE for anyone extending this module: it logs nothing on purpose — a pure
57	# registry has nothing to report, since validation RAISES and generation is
58	# deterministic. If that ever changes, take the logger from
59	# `logging.getLogger("doxyguard_db")` directly and NOT from `._common`, which
60	# would pull `rich` into every importer (see the module docstring on leafness).
61	
62	
63	## @brief A declared config value outside its schema vocabulary.
64	## @version 1
65	class DeclarationError(ValueError):
66	    """Raised at declaration-load time when a repo's `.doxyguard-db.yaml` (or a
67	    standalone manifest) names a token no vocabulary allows.
68	
69	    Deliberately NOT normalized away: the alternative is a build that succeeds
70	    while asserting a synchronization or dispatch fact its author never wrote.
71	    The message carries the origin file, the offending token and the full
72	    allowed set, so the fix is mechanical.
73	
74	    @brief Declared token outside its vocabulary — fail closed.
75	    @version 1
76	    """
77	
78	
79	## @brief Name the manifest a declared value came from, for an error message.
80	## @param source The manifest as a loader received it: a path, a mapping, or None.
81	## @param section The `.doxyguard-db.yaml` section a mapping would have come from.
82	## @return The file path when the loader was given one, else the section name.
83	## @version 2
84	## @req REQ-DDB-SCHEMA-012
85	def declaration_origin(source: object, section: str) -> str:
86	    """A `DeclarationError` is only actionable if it names the file to edit, and
87	    the loaders receive either a standalone manifest path or an already-parsed
88	    `.doxyguard-db.yaml` section — this collapses both into one label.
89	
90	    @brief Label a declaration's origin for a fail-closed error message.
91	    @version 2
92	    """
93	    if isinstance(source, (str, Path)):
94	        return str(source)
95	    return f".doxyguard-db.yaml [{section}]"
96	
97	
98	## @brief One enumerated value set: its members, meaning, and per-value rank.
99	## @version 1
100	@dataclass(frozen=True)
101	class Vocabulary:
102	    """An enumerated column's allowed values plus the semantics a consumer needs
103	    to read them.
104	
105	    `values` is ORDERED and the order is part of the emitted schema text.
106	    `rank` is an EXPLICIT per-value map, never derived from position: `call_match`
107	    is ordered strongest-first (exact, resolved, fuzzy) while every strength
108	    vocabulary is ordered weakest-first (low, medium, high), so a positional
109	    ordinal would invert one of them.
110	    `reserved` marks values the CHECK permits but no code path writes — allowed
111	    so the schema stays forward-compatible, and flagged so a test asserting
112	    "every value is observed in data" does not have to fail.
113	
114	    @brief One enumerated value set (members + meaning + rank).
115	    @version 1
116	    """
117	
118	    id: str
119	    values: tuple[str, ...]
120	    means: str
121	    rank: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
122	    reserved: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
123	
124	    ## @brief SQL CHECK clause constraining a column to this vocabulary.
125	    ## @param column Name of the column the clause guards.
126	    ## @return A `CHECK(col IN (...))` fragment, valid for any arity >= 1.
127	    ## @version 1
128	    ## @req REQ-DDB-SCHEMA-012
129	    def check(self, column: str) -> str:
130	        """Explicit quote-and-join, never `{tuple!r}` — a 1-tuple repr carries a
131	        trailing comma that SQLite rejects, and repr quotes an apostrophe-bearing
132	        value with double quotes, which SQLite reads as an identifier.
133	
134	        @brief Generate this vocabulary's CHECK clause for one column.
135	        @version 1
136	        """
137	        inner = ", ".join("'" + v.replace("'", "''") + "'" for v in self.values)
138	        return f"CHECK({column} IN ({inner}))"
139	
140	    ## @brief Membership test, so `token in vocabulary` reads naturally.
141	    ## @param value Candidate token.
142	    ## @return True when the token is one of this vocabulary's values.
143	    ## @version 1
144	    ## @dg_internal
145	    def __contains__(self, value: object) -> bool:
146	        """@brief True when `value` is a member of this vocabulary.
147	
148	        @version 1
149	        """
150	        return value in self.values
151	
152	    ## @brief Return a declared token when allowed, else raise DeclarationError.
153	    ## @param value The token as declared.
154	    ## @param owner Where it was declared (file + entry), for the message.
155	    ## @param field Field name it was declared under, for the message.
156	    ## @return The value, unchanged.
157	    ## @version 1
158	    ## @req REQ-DDB-SCHEMA-012
159	    def validated(self, value: str, *, owner: str, field: str) -> str:
160	        """The single choke point every declared-enum path routes through. It
161	        raises rather than falling back because there is no honest fallback: see
162	        the module docstring on lock identity collapse.
163	
164	        @brief Validate one declared token, failing closed.
165	        @version 1
166	        """
167	        if value in self.values:
168	            return value
169	        raise DeclarationError(
170	            f"{owner}: invalid {field} {value!r} — allowed: {', '.join(self.values)}"
171	        )
172	
173	
174	# ── The registry ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
175	# One entry per distinct MEANING, even where two entries carry identical tuples.
176	
177	## The six call-edge provenance layers, named because six sites already import
178	## three of them from `call_edges` (which re-exports these, keeping its own
179	## per-layer commentary next to the code that produces each). Spelling them once
180	## here is what stops a value from existing in the CHECK but not the constant, or
181	## the reverse.
182	CALL_SOURCE_DOXYGEN_SQLITE = "doxygen_sqlite"
183	CALL_SOURCE_AST = "ast"
184	CALL_SOURCE_AST_MEMBER = "ast_member"
185	CALL_SOURCE_FNPTR = "fnptr"
186	## The one provenance no call site names. Every other layer OBSERVES a call and
187	## argues about how precisely it resolved; this one is an author's declaration
188	## that an indirection (a virtual seam, a function-pointer table) connects two
189	## functions the source text keeps apart. Separable on purpose — a consumer must
190	## always be able to ask "would this edge exist without the manifest?".
191	CALL_SOURCE_DECLARED_DISPATCH = "declared_dispatch"
192	## A call the source text makes THROUGH A MACRO, composed from the two hops doxygen
193	## already records: `caller → macro definition` and `macro definition → callee`.
194	##
195	## Separate from `doxygen_sqlite` although it comes from the same `xrefs` table, because
196	## it is the only edge here whose two endpoints never appear together at any call site —
197	## the composition is ours, and a consumer must be able to ask "did doxygen say this
198	## directly, or did we join it?". Measured cause: a C accessor convention expressed
199	## entirely as function-like macros produced ZERO outgoing call edges for every macro-only
200	## caller, because both importers require BOTH endpoints to be `kind='function'` and a
201	## `#define` is `kind='macro definition'`. Turning on the preprocessor does NOT fix it —
202	## measured as a no-op on every metric; the hops were always there and we discarded them.
203	CALL_SOURCE_MACRO_HOP = "macro_hop"
204	## A function reference BOUND rather than called: `handler = do_work` or, in Python,
205	## `sub.set_defaults(func=cmd_rubric)`. The binding is plainly in the source text, but
206	## no layer that looks for a CALL can see it, so the caller side of every such
207	## dispatch was empty — argparse subcommands being the measured case (gh#1).
208	##
209	## Separable from `ast` on purpose, and the distinction is real rather than
210	## bookkeeping: `ast` means a call site was OBSERVED at that line, while this means a
211	## reference was handed to someone else who will call it, at a time and on a thread
212	## this edge says nothing about. A consumer summarising control flow must be able to
213	## tell "X calls Y here" from "X arranges for Y to be called later".
214	CALL_SOURCE_BINDING = "binding"
215	
216	CALL_SOURCE = Vocabulary(
217	    id="call_source",
218	    values=(
219	        CALL_SOURCE_DOXYGEN_SQLITE,
220	        CALL_SOURCE_AST,
221	        CALL_SOURCE_AST_MEMBER,
222	        CALL_SOURCE_FNPTR,
223	        CALL_SOURCE_DECLARED_DISPATCH,
224	        CALL_SOURCE_MACRO_HOP,
225	        CALL_SOURCE_BINDING,
226	    ),
227	    means="which extraction layer produced this call edge",
228	    # Ranked ABOVE doxygen's own exact xrefs: the others are inferences graded by
229	    # how well a name resolved, while a declared edge is a statement of fact by
230	    # the person who wrote the indirection. That it is synthetic is carried by
231	    # the source VALUE, which a consumer reads directly — not by demoting it.
232	    ## `macro_hop` sits just BELOW doxygen's direct xrefs and above every name-resolving
233	    ## inference. Both of its hops are doxygen's own observations, so it is stronger than
234	    ## anything that matched on a name — but the COMPOSITION is ours, so it must not
235	    ## outrank an edge doxygen stated directly.
236	    ## Renumbered 0-6 when `macro_hop` was inserted, and 0-7 when `binding` was.
237	    ## Only the ORDER is load-bearing — `_collapse_variants` compares ranks to pick
238	    ## which layer's provenance a collapsed row reports — so the absolute values carry
239	    ## no meaning and gaps buy nothing.
240	    ##
241	    ## `binding` sits BELOW `ast` and above `ast_member`. Below `ast` because when a
242	    ## function is both called outright and bound somewhere, the observed call is the
243	    ## better description of the pair. Above `ast_member` because a binding names a
244	    ## bare identifier and so was never guessed from an unwrapped tail.
245	    rank={
246	        CALL_SOURCE_DECLARED_DISPATCH: 7,
247	        CALL_SOURCE_DOXYGEN_SQLITE: 6,
248	        CALL_SOURCE_MACRO_HOP: 4,
249	        CALL_SOURCE_AST: 3,
250	        CALL_SOURCE_BINDING: 2,
251	        CALL_SOURCE_AST_MEMBER: 1,
252	        CALL_SOURCE_FNPTR: 0,
253	    },
254	)
255	
256	## The two tiers every NAME-resolving layer files an edge under — a single
257	## matching definition vs several candidates. Named because four producers now
258	## write them (AST Layer 3, the fnptr Layer 4, the ast_member recovery and the
259	## declared-dispatch Layer 6) and the weaker tier is load-bearing beyond
260	## provenance: `mark_reachability` and thread membership BOTH skip 'fuzzy', so
261	## mis-spelling it in a producer silently promotes a guess into the liveness BFS.
262	CALL_MATCH_EXACT = "exact"
263	CALL_MATCH_RESOLVED = "resolved"
264	CALL_MATCH_FUZZY = "fuzzy"
265	
266	CALL_MATCH = Vocabulary(
267	    id="call_match",
268	    values=(CALL_MATCH_EXACT, CALL_MATCH_RESOLVED, CALL_MATCH_FUZZY),
269	    means="how precisely the callee rowid was resolved (NOT how likely the call is real)",
270	    rank={CALL_MATCH_EXACT: 2, CALL_MATCH_RESOLVED: 1, CALL_MATCH_FUZZY: 0},
271	)
272	
273	KEY_SOURCE = Vocabulary(
274	    id="key_source",
275	    values=("shared_key_inferred", "shared_key_declared"),
276	    means="whether a dataflow edge came from accessor inference or a manifest",
277	    rank={"shared_key_declared": 1, "shared_key_inferred": 0},
278	)
279	
280	KEY_STRENGTH = Vocabulary(
281	    id="key_strength",
282	    values=("low", "medium", "high"),
283	    means="confidence that a shared-key write/read pair really is a dataflow seam",
284	    rank={"low": 0, "medium": 1, "high": 2},
285	    reserved=frozenset({"low"}),
286	)
287	
288	EDGE_KIND = Vocabulary(
289	    id="edge_kind",
290	    values=("state", "event", "unknown"),
291	    means="whether the key carries retained state or a fire-once event",
292	    rank={"state": 0, "event": 0, "unknown": 0},
293	)
294	
295	DISPATCH_MODE = Vocabulary(
296	    id="dispatch_mode",
297	    values=("inline", "queued", "keyed", "unknown"),
298	    means="the synchrony class of the hand-off: same-thread, buffered, or topic-routed",
299	    rank={"inline": 0, "queued": 0, "keyed": 0, "unknown": 0},
300	)
301	
302	## Python's spawn primitives forced TWO new members rather than reusing the
303	## nearest existing one, because this column is what a consumer reads to decide
304	## whether two functions can race.
305	##   - `process` (`multiprocessing.Process`): a separate ADDRESS SPACE. Filing it
306	##     as 'pthread' or 'task' would say the two share memory, so a consumer would
307	##     hunt for a lock on state that is copy-on-fork and cannot be shared at all.
308	##   - `coroutine` (`asyncio.create_task`): cooperative, on the SAME OS thread.
309	##     Filing it as 'pthread' invents a preemption boundary — a consumer would
310	##     report a data race between two coroutines that can only interleave at
311	##     `await`, which is the opposite of the truth.
312	## `threading.Thread` stays 'pthread' (CPython on POSIX really does create one),
313	## and a pool `submit` stays 'task' (a work item scheduled onto a pool).
314	THREAD_KIND_PROCESS = "process"
315	THREAD_KIND_COROUTINE = "coroutine"
316	
317	## `win32` forced a new member for the SAME reason `process` and `coroutine` did: the two
318	## nearest existing values would each assert something untrue, and this column is what a
319	## consumer reads to decide whether two functions can race.
320	##   - 'pthread' names a POSIX primitive. `_beginthread` / `CreateThread` are not one, and a
321	##     reader who greps for `pthread_` on that label finds nothing and concludes the row is
322	##     wrong.
323	##   - 'task' names a work item scheduled onto an RTOS or a pool. A Win32 thread is a real
324	##     preemptible OS thread with its own stack, which is a stronger claim than 'task' makes.
325	## Both would still get the RACE question right; the label would simply be a lie about the
326	## API, and this project has already learned that a plausible label is quoted onward.
327	THREAD_KIND_WIN32 = "win32"
328	
329	_THREAD_KINDS = (
330	    "task",
331	    "pthread",
332	    THREAD_KIND_WIN32,
333	    "timer",
334	    "isr",
335	    "main",
336	    "oneshot",
337	    THREAD_KIND_PROCESS,
338	    THREAD_KIND_COROUTINE,
339	    "unknown",
340	)
341	
342	THREAD_KIND = Vocabulary(
343	    id="thread_kind",
344	    ## ONE TUPLE, read twice. `values` and `rank` were two hand-maintained copies of the same
345	    ## list, so adding a member meant remembering to edit both — and a value present in
346	    ## `values` but absent from `rank` is exactly the shape that produces a KeyError on a
347	    ## payload path rather than at import.
348	    values=_THREAD_KINDS,
349	    means="the execution-context primitive this thread was spawned as",
350	    rank=dict.fromkeys(_THREAD_KINDS, 0),
351	)
352	
353	THREAD_SOURCE = Vocabulary(

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""The schema's enumerated vocabularies — ONE definition per value set.

Every enumerated column in docs.db used to spell its allowed values as a SQL
string literal at the CREATE TABLE site, and sometimes a SECOND time as a module
constant guarding the declared-config path. That is 25 literals across 8 modules
with nothing tying them together, and it had already drifted: `_VALID_KINDS` was
defined TWICE with DIFFERENT values (`threads.py`, a set of thread kinds;
`locks.py`, a tuple of lock kinds), so a cross-import would have produced a
silently wrong CHECK on whichever table lost the race.

This module is the single source. A column's allowed values live in exactly one
`Vocabulary`; the DDL asks it for a clause (`check(table, column)`) and the
declared-config loaders ask the SAME object to validate a token.

TRUE LEAF — zero intra-package imports, by design. `doxyguard_db/_common.py`
pulls in `rich`, while `doxyguard_db/query/_common.py` is deliberately
stdlib-only; importing either here would make one of those two layers
un-importable without the other's dependencies. The logger comes from `logging`
directly for exactly that reason.

FIVE VOCABULARIES SHARE THE TUPLE ('low','medium','high') AND ARE STILL FIVE
OBJECTS. They mean five different things — spawn-detection strength, inferred-
vs-declared provenance, lock-identity certainty, acquisition-resolution success,
and a constant on `external_boundaries`. Binding one object to all five would
mean that adding a value for one silently widens the CHECK on the other four,
while every test that compares the shipped schema to this registry stays green.

GENERATION NEVER USES `{tuple!r}`. The idiom this replaces (`locks.py`) emits
`CHECK(c IN ('x',))` for a one-value set — a SQLite SYNTAX ERROR — and
`CHECK(c IN ("it's",))` for a value containing an apostrophe. It survived only
by accident, because every set it was applied to happened to have >= 2 values;
`boundary_source` had exactly one until the declared-dispatch terminus kind
landed, which is precisely how a latent one-value case reaches production.
`values` is also a TUPLE, never a set: set iteration order is not part of any
contract, and a set here would make the shipped schema text vary between builds.

FAIL CLOSED on a declared value outside its vocabulary (`validated` raises
`DeclarationError`), rather than normalizing to 'unknown' as the loaders used
to. `acq_form`/`acq_role`/`acq_mode` have no 'unknown' member at all, so a
fallback has to invent a specific, real synchronization claim out of a typo. And
`locks.kind` is part of lock IDENTITY (`UNIQUE(name, scope, kind)`), so two
differently-typo'd kinds normalizing to one token COLLAPSE INTO ONE lock row —
fabricating shared synchronization, which is precisely the error the lock layer
documents itself as failing closed against.

@brief Central registry of the schema's enumerated value sets.
@version 3
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

# NOTE for anyone extending this module: it logs nothing on purpose — a pure
# registry has nothing to report, since validation RAISES and generation is
# deterministic. If that ever changes, take the logger from
# `logging.getLogger("doxyguard_db")` directly and NOT from `._common`, which
# would pull `rich` into every importer (see the module docstring on leafness).


## @brief A declared config value outside its schema vocabulary.
## @version 1
class DeclarationError(ValueError):
    """Raised at declaration-load time when a repo's `.doxyguard-db.yaml` (or a
    standalone manifest) names a token no vocabulary allows.

    Deliberately NOT normalized away: the alternative is a build that succeeds
    while asserting a synchronization or dispatch fact its author never wrote.
    The message carries the origin file, the offending token and the full
    allowed set, so the fix is mechanical.

    @brief Declared token outside its vocabulary — fail closed.
    @version 1
    """


## @brief Name the manifest a declared value came from, for an error message.
## @param source The manifest as a loader received it: a path, a mapping, or None.
## @param section The `.doxyguard-db.yaml` section a mapping would have come from.
## @return The file path when the loader was given one, else the section name.
## @version 2
## @req REQ-DDB-SCHEMA-012
def declaration_origin(source: object, section: str) -> str:
    """A `DeclarationError` is only actionable if it names the file to edit, and
    the loaders receive either a standalone manifest path or an already-parsed
    `.doxyguard-db.yaml` section — this collapses both into one label.

    @brief Label a declaration's origin for a fail-closed error message.
    @version 2
    """
    if isinstance(source, (str, Path)):
        return str(source)
    return f".doxyguard-db.yaml [{section}]"


## @brief One enumerated value set: its members, meaning, and per-value rank.
## @version 1
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Vocabulary:
    """An enumerated column's allowed values plus the semantics a consumer needs
    to read them.

    `values` is ORDERED and the order is part of the emitted schema text.
    `rank` is an EXPLICIT per-value map, never derived from position: `call_match`
    is ordered strongest-first (exact, resolved, fuzzy) while every strength
    vocabulary is ordered weakest-first (low, medium, high), so a positional
    ordinal would invert one of them.
    `reserved` marks values the CHECK permits but no code path writes — allowed
    so the schema stays forward-compatible, and flagged so a test asserting
    "every value is observed in data" does not have to fail.

    @brief One enumerated value set (members + meaning + rank).
    @version 1
    """

    id: str
    values: tuple[str, ...]
    means: str
    rank: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    reserved: frozenset[str] = frozenset()

    ## @brief SQL CHECK clause constraining a column to this vocabulary.
    ## @param column Name of the column the clause guards.
    ## @return A `CHECK(col IN (...))` fragment, valid for any arity >= 1.
    ## @version 1
    ## @req REQ-DDB-SCHEMA-012
    def check(self, column: str) -> str:
        """Explicit quote-and-join, never `{tuple!r}` — a 1-tuple repr carries a
        trailing comma that SQLite rejects, and repr quotes an apostrophe-bearing
        value with double quotes, which SQLite reads as an identifier.

        @brief Generate this vocabulary's CHECK clause for one column.
        @version 1
        """
        inner = ", ".join("'" + v.replace("'", "''") + "'" for v in self.values)
        return f"CHECK({column} IN ({inner}))"

    ## @brief Membership test, so `token in vocabulary` reads naturally.
    ## @param value Candidate token.
    ## @return True when the token is one of this vocabulary's values.
    ## @version 1
    ## @dg_internal
    def __contains__(self, value: object) -> bool:
        """@brief True when `value` is a member of this vocabulary.

        @version 1
        """
        return value in self.values

    ## @brief Return a declared token when allowed, else raise DeclarationError.
    ## @param value The token as declared.
    ## @param owner Where it was declared (file + entry), for the message.
    ## @param field Field name it was declared under, for the message.
    ## @return The value, unchanged.
    ## @version 1
    ## @req REQ-DDB-SCHEMA-012
    def validated(self, value: str, *, owner: str, field: str) -> str:
        """The single choke point every declared-enum path routes through. It
        raises rather than falling back because there is no honest fallback: see
        the module docstring on lock identity collapse.

        @brief Validate one declared token, failing closed.
        @version 1
        """
        if value in self.values:
            return value
        raise DeclarationError(
            f"{owner}: invalid {field} {value!r} — allowed: {', '.join(self.values)}"
        )


# ── The registry ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One entry per distinct MEANING, even where two entries carry identical tuples.

## The six call-edge provenance layers, named because six sites already import
## three of them from `call_edges` (which re-exports these, keeping its own
## per-layer commentary next to the code that produces each). Spelling them once
## here is what stops a value from existing in the CHECK but not the constant, or
## the reverse.
CALL_SOURCE_DOXYGEN_SQLITE = "doxygen_sqlite"
CALL_SOURCE_AST = "ast"
CALL_SOURCE_AST_MEMBER = "ast_member"
CALL_SOURCE_FNPTR = "fnptr"
## The one provenance no call site names. Every other layer OBSERVES a call and
## argues about how precisely it resolved; this one is an author's declaration
## that an indirection (a virtual seam, a function-pointer table) connects two
## functions the source text keeps apart. Separable on purpose — a consumer must
## always be able to ask "would this edge exist without the manifest?".
CALL_SOURCE_DECLARED_DISPATCH = "declared_dispatch"
## A call the source text makes THROUGH A MACRO, composed from the two hops doxygen
## already records: `caller → macro definition` and `macro definition → callee`.
##
## Separate from `doxygen_sqlite` although it comes from the same `xrefs` table, because
## it is the only edge here whose two endpoints never appear together at any call site —
## the composition is ours, and a consumer must be able to ask "did doxygen say this
## directly, or did we join it?". Measured cause: a C accessor convention expressed
## entirely as function-like macros produced ZERO outgoing call edges for every macro-only
## caller, because both importers require BOTH endpoints to be `kind='function'` and a
## `#define` is `kind='macro definition'`. Turning on the preprocessor does NOT fix it —
## measured as a no-op on every metric; the hops were always there and we discarded them.
CALL_SOURCE_MACRO_HOP = "macro_hop"
## A function reference BOUND rather than called: `handler = do_work` or, in Python,
## `sub.set_defaults(func=cmd_rubric)`. The binding is plainly in the source text, but
## no layer that looks for a CALL can see it, so the caller side of every such
## dispatch was empty — argparse subcommands being the measured case (gh#1).
##
## Separable from `ast` on purpose, and the distinction is real rather than
## bookkeeping: `ast` means a call site was OBSERVED at that line, while this means a
## reference was handed to someone else who will call it, at a time and on a thread
## this edge says nothing about. A consumer summarising control flow must be able to
## tell "X calls Y here" from "X arranges for Y to be called later".
CALL_SOURCE_BINDING = "binding"

CALL_SOURCE = Vocabulary(
    id="call_source",
    values=(
        CALL_SOURCE_DOXYGEN_SQLITE,
        CALL_SOURCE_AST,
        CALL_SOURCE_AST_MEMBER,
        CALL_SOURCE_FNPTR,
        CALL_SOURCE_DECLARED_DISPATCH,
        CALL_SOURCE_MACRO_HOP,
        CALL_SOURCE_BINDING,
    ),
    means="which extraction layer produced this call edge",
    # Ranked ABOVE doxygen's own exact xrefs: the others are inferences graded by
    # how well a name resolved, while a declared edge is a statement of fact by
    # the person who wrote the indirection. That it is synthetic is carried by
    # the source VALUE, which a consumer reads directly — not by demoting it.
    ## `macro_hop` sits just BELOW doxygen's direct xrefs and above every name-resolving
    ## inference. Both of its hops are doxygen's own observations, so it is stronger than
    ## anything that matched on a name — but the COMPOSITION is ours, so it must not
    ## outrank an edge doxygen stated directly.
    ## Renumbered 0-6 when `macro_hop` was inserted, and 0-7 when `binding` was.
    ## Only the ORDER is load-bearing — `_collapse_variants` compares ranks to pick
    ## which layer's provenance a collapsed row reports — so the absolute values carry
    ## no meaning and gaps buy nothing.
    ##
    ## `binding` sits BELOW `ast` and above `ast_member`. Below `ast` because when a
    ## function is both called outright and bound somewhere, the observed call is the
    ## better description of the pair. Above `ast_member` because a binding names a
    ## bare identifier and so was never guessed from an unwrapped tail.
    rank={
        CALL_SOURCE_DECLARED_DISPATCH: 7,
        CALL_SOURCE_DOXYGEN_SQLITE: 6,
        CALL_SOURCE_MACRO_HOP: 4,
        CALL_SOURCE_AST: 3,
        CALL_SOURCE_BINDING: 2,
        CALL_SOURCE_AST_MEMBER: 1,
        CALL_SOURCE_FNPTR: 0,
    },
)

## The two tiers every NAME-resolving layer files an edge under — a single
## matching definition vs several candidates. Named because four producers now
## write them (AST Layer 3, the fnptr Layer 4, the ast_member recovery and the
## declared-dispatch Layer 6) and the weaker tier is load-bearing beyond
## provenance: `mark_reachability` and thread membership BOTH skip 'fuzzy', so
## mis-spelling it in a producer silently promotes a guess into the liveness BFS.
CALL_MATCH_EXACT = "exact"
CALL_MATCH_RESOLVED = "resolved"
CALL_MATCH_FUZZY = "fuzzy"

CALL_MATCH = Vocabulary(
    id="call_match",

## symbol's rowid), and this column says WHY it is NULL.

## has no member for "no memberdef exists at all" — the majority case here, since
## a critical section is full of stdlib, vendor and macro calls. Reusing it would

## when in truth there was never a candidate. And 'exact' is unreachable for L2:

## Kconfig's own universal convention rather than assuming a repo's shape. True for a
## Kconfig repo, and it made the layer INERT on the dominant C convention: mbedtls gates
## everything on `#if defined(MBEDTLS_THREADING_C)` and declares its space in a checked-in
## `mbedtls_config.h`, so the table existed with the right columns and held ZERO rows on a
## 500-file repository whose whole question is "what is compiled in".
##
## So the harvest records EVERY symbol a preprocessor conditional gates on, and this says
## how that name was accounted for. Classification, never filtering — a repository that has
## adopted nothing still gets a complete gate layer, which is the third-party case the
## declaration model exists to serve.
##   - 'kconfig'    — carries Kconfig's `CONFIG_` prefix.
##   - 'declared'   — named by the target's own preprocessor declaration (a config header
##     or an explicit predefined list). This is the variant the index REPRESENTS.

## @param table Table the column belongs to.
## @param column Column name.
## @return A `CHECK(col IN (...))` fragment ready to splice into a CREATE TABLE.
## @version 1
## @req REQ-DDB-SCHEMA-012
def check(table: str, column: str) -> str:
    """Raises rather than returning an empty string for an unregistered column:
    a silently-absent CHECK is the exact hole this module exists to close.

    @brief Look up a column's vocabulary and generate its CHECK clause.
    @version 1

    vocab = COLUMNS.get((table, column))

## @param column Column name.
## @return A `CHECK(col IN (0,1))` fragment.
## @version 1
## @req REQ-DDB-SCHEMA-012

  1. A FILESYSTEM SOURCE SCAN forbidding a raw `CHECK(` literal anywhere in the
     package outside `vocabulary.py`. No artifact-based test can replace it: a
     hand-rolled CHECK inside a CREATE TABLE that the fixture build never
     executes is invisible to any reconcile against a shipped database
     (`enrichment.architecture_topics` is created only under `--enrich` and
     exists in none of the databases on this machine). It scans via
     `pathlib.rglob`, NOT `git ls-files`, because the gate is blind to untracked
     files — that is exactly how `htmlview.py` once landed 10 violations after a
     green run.

  2. A COMMITTED GOLDEN SNAPSHOT (`tests/data/schema_vocabulary.json`) compared
     against a freshly built schema. Comparing the shipped CHECK to the registry
     that GENERATED it passes by construction for any value set, so widening a
     vocabulary would be undetectable. The snapshot is an external baseline a
     human has to deliberately edit.

  3. GENERATOR EDGE CASES that the idiom this replaces got wrong — a one-value
     vocabulary, an apostrophe-bearing value, and byte-stability across
     interpreter processes with different hash seeds.

@brief Vocabulary registry, generated-CHECK, and source-scan tests.
@version 1
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from schema_snapshot import parse_checks

from doxyguard_db.call_edges import build_call_edges

from doxyguard_db.shared_key_edges import _ensure_shared_key_edges_table

    ACQ_STRENGTH,
    BOOL_COLUMNS,
    BOUNDARY_KIND,
    BOUNDARY_SOURCE,
    BOUNDARY_STRENGTH,
    CALL_SOURCE,
    CALL_SOURCE_DECLARED_DISPATCH,
    COLUMNS,
    KEY_STRENGTH,
    LOCK_IDENTITY,
    THREAD_KIND,
    THREAD_STRENGTH,
    VOCABULARIES,

)

PACKAGE = REPO / "doxyguard_db"
SNAPSHOT = REPO / "tests" / "data" / "schema_vocabulary.json"


# ─── 1. source scans: the only thing that stops a future bypass ──────────────


## @brief Every .py file in the shipped package, found on the FILESYSTEM.
## @return Package sources, excluding compiled bytecode directories.
## @version 1
def _package_sources() -> list[Path]:
    """rglob, not `git ls-files`: the git-aware gate cannot see an untracked
    file, which is how a new module once landed 10 standards violations after a
    green `pre-commit --all-files` run.

    @brief Walk the package on disk, git state irrelevant.
    @version 1
    """
    return [p for p in PACKAGE.rglob("*.py") if "__pycache__" not in p.parts]

    """The whole point of the module: `CHECK(` may appear in exactly ONE file.

    An artifact reconcile cannot catch a hand-rolled CHECK in a CREATE TABLE the
    fixture build never runs, and `pre-commit --all-files` cannot see a brand-new
    untracked file at all. This scan sees both.

    offenders = [
        str(path.relative_to(REPO))
        for path in _package_sources()
        if path.name != "vocabulary.py" and "CHECK(" in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    ]
    assert offenders == [], (
        f"raw CHECK( literal outside vocabulary.py in {offenders} — "
        "generate it with vocabulary.check(table, column) / bool_check(column)"
    )

    package including the two subpackages a `**` pathspec silently skips."""

    wrong CHECK. After the migration no module defines any `_VALID_` constant,

    ## fixture's own tests while the real build shipped something else.
